text_blocks.snippet: The Section 45Q tax credit is a federal incentive designed to encourage carbon capture and storage (CCS) and carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) projects. It provides a tax credit per metric ton of qualified carbon oxide captured and sequestered or utilized. The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 significantly increased the value of the 45Q credit and expanded its applicability.
snippet_highlighted_words: a federal incentive designed to encourage carbon capture and storage (CCS) and carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) projects

text_blocks.snippet: Key Aspects of the 45Q Tax Credit:

list.title: Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS):
list.snippet: The credit incentivizes the capture and permanent storage of carbon oxides (like CO2) in geological formations.

list.title: Carbon Capture and Utilization (CCUS):
list.snippet: The credit also applies to the capture and use of carbon oxides in various processes, including enhanced oil recovery (EOR) and manufacturing of low-carbon products.

list.title: Direct Air Capture (DAC):
list.snippet: The 45Q credit also applies to DAC facilities, which directly capture CO2 from the atmosphere.

list.title: Increased Credit Values:
list.snippet: The Inflation Reduction Act increased the credit amounts, with a maximum of $85 per tonne for geological storage and $180 per tonne for DAC facilities.

list.title: Prevailing Wage Requirements:
list.snippet: The credit amounts can be multiplied by five if certain prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements are met during the construction, alteration, or repair of the emitting facility and carbon capture equipment, according to EisnerAmper.

list.title: Minimum Capture Amounts:
list.snippet: Facilities must meet minimum annual capture requirements to be eligible for the credit.

list.title: MRV Plans:
list.snippet: Companies must have approved Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) plans for the captured CO2, according to the Carbon Capture Coalition.

list.title: 1. Capture:
list.snippet: Carbon oxides are captured from industrial facilities, power plants, or directly from the atmosphere (DAC).

list.title: 2. Storage or Utilization:
list.snippet: The captured CO2 is either stored geologically or utilized in a qualified manner.

list.title: 3. Measurement and Reporting:
list.snippet: Companies measure the captured CO2 and report it to the EPA's Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (GHGRP), according to the Carbon Capture Coalition.

list.title: 4. Tax Credit Claim:
list.snippet: Companies claim the 45Q tax credit based on the amount of CO2 captured and stored or utilized.

text_blocks.snippet: Impact of the Inflation Reduction Act:

The Inflation Reduction Act significantly increased the value of the 45Q tax credit, making it a more attractive incentive for carbon capture and storage projects. This is expected to accelerate the deployment of CCS and CCUS technologies, helping to reduce carbon emissions, according to Clean Air Task Force.
